blocks: Artist who made audiokinetic sculptures: rolling-ball machines with bells and chimes.

(1926–2021), renowned for his Sound/Sculpture/Audiokinetic audiokinetic sculptures featuring rolling balls, bells, chimes, and intricate mechanical pathways. One of his most notable works, 42nd Street Ballroom, has been installed at the Port Authority Bus Terminal in New York City since 1983. This 8-foot cube captivates passersby with 24 billiard balls navigating four distinct tracks, activating over 15 devices that produce various sounds and movements
American jazz composer, arranger and theorist (1923–2009).
His Lydian Chromatic Concept of Tonal Organization (1953) set out a theory of harmony based on jazz.

German psychologist, born 3 September 1947 in Wallersdorf, emeritus director at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development and director of the Harding Center for Risk Literacy at the University of Potsdam.
Studies bounded rationality and heuristics: how people infer and decide with limited time and knowledge.

Co-author, with Peter M. Todd and the ABC Research Group, of Simple Heuristics That Make Us Smart (Oxford University Press, 1999), on fast and frugal heuristics as a model of bounded rationality: Satis/fice.
Role: Writer and host, Person/Gergely Orosz/Podcast
